label: early copy phase, upcoming output j
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of mass; never on original inputs or the <DEL> step itself), mostly at early recall positions 1-3 (recall_idx 2 has the highest rate, 20%). The strongest driver is an original j that is being output now or within the next few steps: out_tok=j has 10x lift and next_out=j 11x, and top activations are steps just before or at a run of j outputs (e.g. s j j j e <DEL> s* j*). Weaker lift for other upcoming outputs g, z, e, 0, 2, t. Low-level activations are spread diffusely over early copy steps with no j nearby, so a predicate built on upcoming j has F1 ~0.48 on dev (precision 0.61, recall 0.39, mass recall 0.59). Broadening to the token set {j,g,z,e,0,2,t} raises mass recall to 0.87 but cuts precision to 0.2.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: j, g, z, e, 0, 2; least: x, l, v, d) and the next token to output (most: j, e, g, z, t, h; least: x, s, d, l); timing cues that raise it most: phase=2, recall_idx=2, recall_idx=1.
